valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 20 Nov 2026. (1) Business: one main business, coconut-shell activated carbon (99% of 2025/26 operating profit, note 36), plus a small water-engineering arm (Puritas), so one sector beta. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) could NOT be opened (his site isn't reachable from this run). Stand-in from a web-search extract of his global table: Chemical (Specialty), unlevered and cash-corrected, 1.04 (date not shown); his US figure for January 2026 is 0.82. (3) Relevered with net debt Rs 25.54bn (30 Sep 2026, incl. leases and the related-party loan, less cash) ÷ market value Rs 66.56bn (297.12mn shares × Rs 224, TradingView snapshot, about mid-November 2026) = 0.38, at the 26.3% effective tax rate: 1.04 × (1 + 0.737 × 0.38) = 1.33. (4) No local 5-year beta found by web search; TradingView shows 1-year betas of 1.08 and 0.95 (ignored as 1-year). (5) So 1.33 is used. (6) Within 0.3–2, but high: with the US sector figure it would be 1.05. (7) Cost of equity from scripts/reinvestment.py. (8) Shown in the Required return tile. Refresh in January 2027.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: scripts/reinvestment.py, 20 Nov 2026: cost of debt 6.54% (interest paid ÷ average borrowings and leases 2025/26), tax 26.3%, debt weight 27.7% at Rs 224. Used only in the DCF cross-check.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 3% / 7% / 10%; supported 52.4% by the calculator, 8.2% on profit kept × ROE
valuationInputs.reason: The calculator's figure comes from a 2025/26 reinvestment rate of 323% (a Rs 13.4bn working-capital build) and is not meaningful. Profit kept × ROE (66.6% × 12.3%) = 8.2%: all scenarios within 2 points; the bull is supported by the Philippines plant (+7,500 MT, about 13% more capacity, from 2027/28).

valuationInputs.name: Maintenance capex basis
valuationInputs.reason: No company split. 2025/26 capex booked Rs 4.33bn of which the report names Rs 2.69bn as capacity expansion (energy-storage and value-added carbons); the rest (Rs 1.64bn) is close to depreciation and amortisation (Rs 1.21bn). So 2025/26 capex was mostly growth.

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: P/E, justified price to book, residual income (weighted); whole-company DCF as a cross-check
valuationInputs.reason: Operating cash was negative in 2025/26 and H1 2026/27 because of a charcoal stock build, so the DCF needs a normalised start and, with Rs 25.5bn net debt, swings from Rs −45 to Rs 66 a share. Dividends (a third of profit) shown as a reading.

valuationInputs.name: EPS to March 2027
valuationInputs.reason: H1 Rs 8.41 plus a second half of Rs 6.6 / 9.1 / 10.6. Run-rate Rs 18.84 (Sep quarter × 4; last 12 months Rs 16.35): base 7% below it because demand and charcoal prices look like a peak.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Five-year average 17%, ten-year 16% (range 9–26%); last 12 months about 16%.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Roughly nominal GDP growth; below the 12.24% bond yield and WACC.

valuationInputs.name: DCF cross-check inputs
valuationInputs.value: Start cash Rs 3.0 / 5.1 / 6.0bn; after-tax operating profit Rs 4.3 / 5.3 / 6.0bn; growth 3 / 7 / 10%; return on capital 12 / 16 / 19%
valuationInputs.reason: Owners' share (about 85%) of the last 12 months' operating profit without currency gains (Rs 8.5bn) at 26.3% tax, less maintenance capex net of depreciation; working-capital growth charged through reinvestment. Result Rs −45 / 13 / 66 a share, not weighted.

openQuestions: Does the Rs 31.5bn of stock (mostly charcoal bought at high prices) turn back into cash, and does net debt (Rs 25.5bn at Sep 2026) fall?
Gross margin: does the September quarter's 23.8% hold if gold prices or charcoal prices move?
Philippines plant: machinery installed by March 2027, first output in 2027/28, and its total cost (not stated).
Related-party loan: its September balance (Rs 1.8bn at March, not split out in the interim).
Energy-storage carbon sales: any figures on volumes or share of revenue.
Refresh the beta in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file and local 5-year betas; switch to the CSE close once HAYC is in the price file.

changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/add HAYC.N0000). First analysis, from the downloaded annual report 2025/26 and the interims to June and September 2026. Methods: P/E, justified price to book and residual income at a 21.9% cost of equity (beta 1.33, provisional, global specialty-chemicals stand-in); DCF as a cross-check only because operating cash was negative. Business tests 3 of 4 (fails cash): category 2, watch list. Uncertain: price is a TradingView web snapshot (Rs 224), not a CSE close; no local 5-year beta; the related-party loan at September isn't disclosed, so March's Rs 1.825bn is used.
